definitions.meaning: to back a cause is to support or stand up for it
one who takes first prize in a contest

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the verb means support or defend, the noun means a title-holder or victor.

definitions.meaning: a nanny goat is an animal that rams with its head
the dairy product spread on bread or scones

explanation.surface: A children's nurse prepares something to put on the bread at teatime.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsically, a goat that butts is a 'butter'; and the dairy spread is the ordinary sense.

clue.text: Snub good girl in posh sort of accent

parts.note: to snub someone is to cut them dead
lass is a word for a girl

explanation.surface: A well-behaved young woman is cold-shouldered for her refined way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-glass accent is a crisp, very upper-class British way of speaking, likened to sharp-edged crystal.

clue.text: A smallholder in the fruit trade

definitions.text: A smallholder in the fruit trade

parts.words: A smallholder in the fruit trade
parts.note: read not as a small farmer but as something that holds a small quantity of fruit for sale, such as strawberries

explanation.definitionFit: A small basket or box in which soft fruit is sold is literally a 'small holder' of fruit.

clue.text: Man in control of a grounded jumbo

definitions.text: Man in control of a grounded jumbo

parts.words: Man in control of a grounded jumbo
parts.note: suggests the pilot of a jumbo jet on the tarmac, but the jumbo is an elephant, which is always grounded

explanation.definitionFit: The Indian term for an elephant's driver or keeper fits a man controlling an elephant.

definitions.meaning: clad in armour made of linked metal rings

explanation.surface: A letter goes off in a padded envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both sent by post and wearing chain armour, as a knight did.

parts.note: a time yet to come becomes the present moment as soon as it arrives

explanation.definitionFit: Time still to come turns into now when it arrives, so it is present on arrival.

indicators.note: the letters of is done are presented wrongly, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: An inventor has been cheated by someone misrepresenting him.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Alva Edison was the American inventor of the phonograph and a practical light bulb.

clue.text: Protect men's organisation in awkward situation

indicators.note: putting letters into a new order, so protect men's is rearranged

explanation.surface: A society to protect men finds itself in an embarrassing position.
explanation.definitionFit: This borrowed French word names an unexpected mishap or embarrassing moment.

clue.text: A thousand odd times is a lot

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, as in kilo

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters of times are out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A thousand strange occurrences adds up to a great many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' turns TIMES into ISMET. 'lot' is not 'many' but one's lot in life.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot is one's fate or destiny, the meaning of this Arabic-derived word.

parts.note: an organ is a musical instrument
a die is a tool for stamping metal, as in coining

explanation.surface: Use a tool to press a design onto delicate cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fine, stiff, translucent cotton fabric used for dresses and trimmings.

clue.text: House in the Home Counties by the motorway

parts.note: the counties round London lie in the south-east of England, SE
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A house in the commuter belt near London lies beside the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London; the M1 runs north from London, its 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a semi is a semi-detached house, sharing one wall with its neighbour.

indicators.note: following says the drawing piece comes after the note

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
traction is the act of drawing or pulling

explanation.surface: An artist pulls a sketch out after a musical interlude.
explanation.definitionFit: A retraction is the taking back of a statement, a withdrawal of it.

clue.text: Girl seen on river, say, dressed up for celebration

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

indicators.note: dressing up changes how something looks, so the letters of river say are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young woman is spotted on the river in her finery for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed up' looks like part of the picture of the girl in finery, but it signals rearranging 'river, say'; 'seen on' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearly commemoration of an event, such as a wedding, is celebrated.

parts.note: an idiot is a fool
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A foolish person picks a fight with the TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiot box is a slang, rather scornful name for the television set.

definitions.meaning: a narration or account of events
an uncle is a family member, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Someone asks to hear the tale of an uncle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a telling of a story and a kinsman, such as an uncle.

parts.note: not a forester relaxing, but a person playing a woodwind instrument

explanation.definitionFit: A player of the oboe, a woodwind instrument, is a 'wood' man playing music.

definitions.meaning: the theatre, as in treading the ...
company directors together form a governing body

explanation.surface: Theatre directors are said to build the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural word means both the theatrical stage and the governing panels of companies that directors sit on.

clue.text: Possibly found in bar seats, but they're not drinking

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of in and bar seats might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Teetotallers might be found sitting at a bar while abstaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' looks like a hidden-word signal, but 'in' is part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Teetotal people who refuse alcohol are known by this word.

parts.note: suggests a medal pinned to the breast, but means an ornamental pin worn on the necktie

explanation.definitionFit: A decorative pin holding a necktie in place sits on the wearer's chest.

indicators.note: fallen arches have collapsed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor inspects a patient for collapsed foot arches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fallen arches' is the foot condition, but 'fallen' signals that ARCHES is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To search is to look through carefully, a synonym of examining closely.

definitions.meaning: an interjection said to make someone notice

explanation.surface: An exclamation is used to get people to notice.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an appearance or facial expression, and is also called out to draw attention.

clue.text: Team needs space to avoid tackles

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
a step is a short distance, the space of one pace

explanation.surface: A rugby team needs room to dodge opponents' tackles.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep is to dodge, as a rugby runner dodges tackles by stepping sideways.

clue.text: It comes straight from the heart

definitions.text: It comes straight from the heart

parts.words: It comes straight from the heart
parts.note: sounds like heartfelt sincerity, but describes a blood vessel leading out of the heart

explanation.definitionFit: The aorta and other major blood vessels carry blood directly away from the heart.

clue.text: Daughter replaces son in final exams at Cambridge, making a stand

indicators.note: D for daughter swaps in where S for son stood, a substitution signal

parts.note: the Tripos is the honours degree examination at Cambridge University

explanation.surface: A family business sees a daughter take over from a son in Cambridge's finals, making a stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged support for a camera or telescope is a kind of stand.

clue.text: A vote to the other side?

parts.note: a voter marks a ballot paper with a cross

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether casting a ballot means changing parties.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means from one side to the other, as when crossing a road.
